questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability That a Random Variable Lies Within a Bounded Interval
questions.problem:
Compute $P(2<X\le 3)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{21}{x}^{2},\, & 1\le x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X\le 3) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{21}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{63}{x}^{3}]}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{63}(27-8) \\  & =\frac{19}{63}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(X>-3)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{72}{x}^{2},\, & -6\le x\le 0, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>-3) & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}\frac{1}{72}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{216}{x}^{3}]}_{-3}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{216}[(0)^{3}-(-3)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{27}{216} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(X>-1)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{28}({x}^{2}+1),\, & -2\le x\le 2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x>2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>-1) & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}\frac{3}{28}({x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{28}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}+1\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{28}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x]}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{28}([\frac{1}{3}(2)^{3}+(2)]-[\frac{1}{3}(-1)^{3}+(-1)]) \\  & =\frac{3}{28}([\frac{8}{3}+2]-[-\frac{1}{3}-1]) \\  & =\frac{3}{28}\cdot 6 \\  & =\frac{9}{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(X\le -1)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{35}{x}^{2},\, & -2\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x<-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le -1) & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{3}{35}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{35}{x}^{3}]}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[(-1)^{3}-(-2)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}(-1+8) \\  & =\frac{1}{35}\cdot 7 \\  & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(X\ge 2)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{34}({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}),\, & 1\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x>3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 2) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{3}{34}({x}^{3}-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{34}{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{34}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{3}{34}([\frac{1}{4}(3)^{4}-\frac{1}{3}(3)^{3}]-[\frac{1}{4}(2)^{4}-\frac{1}{3}(2)^{3}]) \\  & =\frac{3}{34}([\frac{81}{4}-9]-[4-\frac{8}{3}]) \\  & =\frac{3}{34}\cdot \frac{119}{12} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(X\le 3)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{24}({x}^{2}+1),\, & 1\le x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x<1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & ={\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{24}({x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{24}{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}+1\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{24}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+x]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}[(\frac{{3}^{3}}{3}+3)-(\frac{1}{3}+1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{24}(12-\frac{4}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{24}\cdot \frac{32}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}x(x+1),\, & 0\le x<1, \\ \frac{1}{6}x & 1\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Compute $P(2<X\le 3)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{6}x,\, & 1\le x\le 3, \\ \frac{1}{3} & 3<x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X\le 3) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{6}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{12}{x}^{2}]}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[{3}^{2}-{2}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(9-4) \\  & =\frac{5}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(3<X<4)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2},\, & -1\le x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{9}(x-1) & 1<x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3<X<4) & ={\int }_{3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{9}(x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-x]}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}([\frac{1}{2}(4)^{2}-(4)]-[\frac{1}{2}(3)^{2}-(3)]) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(8-4-\frac{9}{2}+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(\frac{5}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(-1\le X\le 2)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10}({x}^{2}+1),\, & -2\le x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{20} & 1<x\le 9, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1\le X\le 2) & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{10}({x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{20}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+x]}_{-1}^{1}+{[\frac{1}{20}x]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}([\frac{1}{3}(1)^{3}+1]-[\frac{1}{3}(-1)^{3}+(-1)])+\frac{1}{20}(2-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(\frac{8}{3})+\frac{1}{20} \\  & =\frac{4}{15}+\frac{1}{20} \\  & =\frac{19}{60}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Compute $P\left( 1 \lt   X \lt 3 \right)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040290/assets/394c60a510e39043cda5072c0b57a663b200275035d72c15f20c5a257e6c4fc0.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a \lt   X \lt      b) = \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X<3) & ={\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{18}({x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{18}{\int }_{1}^{3}({x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{18}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-x]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}([\frac{1}{3}(3)^{3}-(3)]-[\frac{1}{3}(1)^{3}-(1)]) \\  & =\frac{1}{18}([9-3]-[\frac{1}{3}-1]) \\  & =\frac{1}{18}(6+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{18}\cdot \frac{20}{3} \\  & =\frac{10}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040290/assets/1cd6271fdb46d54db66d2b4f5acd10146f42a0dd64a3326ea7e53e07d4915633.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a \leq X \leq  b) = \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x \lt  2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{2x}{45}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{45}\,{x}^{2}]}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{45}({3}^{2}-{2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{45}\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Compute $P\left( 2 \leq          X \leq          4 \right)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040290/assets/e01b36a6a2b00b47ce36b59d5b3e1a4fea4cbc26b0b7d46d60e40638161982d8.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a \leq        X \leq        b) = \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le X\le 4) & ={\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{9}x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{4}(x-3)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{18}{x}^{2}]}_{2}^{3}+{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-3x]}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}[{3}^{2}-{2}^{2}]+([\frac{1}{2}(4)^{2}-3(4)]-[\frac{1}{2}(3)^{2}-3(3)]) \\  & =\frac{5}{18}-4+\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{14}{18} \\  & =\frac{7}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
